note: Written from each account's public posts as they stood on 2026-09-30. Regenerate when the board moves.

entries.note: The bio is all barricades and the timeline is all kitchen table. What she actually posts is domestic stand-up delivered at full volume — the bit about announcing “I REST MY CASE” to an empty apartment, the running forensic commentary on men sliding into the DMs with four inspirational reels before the flirty one. First place because it reads like someone talking to you, not at a room.
entries.line: playing cards with a makeshift deck of Kraft Singles that I drew the suits and numbers on.

entries.note: A specialist in one joke, pursued past all reason. He posted “wristlace,” then spent days replying to his own bit — “it’s not a lie if enough people start calling it a wristlace,” then “an armoire is where you store your arms.” Second place is a referendum on commitment, and he has it.
entries.line: a necklace for your wrist is called a wristlace

entries.note: Short, clean, and sharpened to a point. The structure is almost always setup-then-blade, and the blade lands somewhere you weren’t protecting. Equally happy being funny about mortality and being completely sincere about accountability, often in the same scroll.
entries.line: i brought baklava to a gun fight and everyone complemented me on my flaky layers before i got shot

entries.note: Sports-bar heckler as a literary form. Red Sox partisanship, Jason Voorhees’ missing goalie gear, and a sincere willingness to start a chant from an adjacent bathroom stall. Most of the output lives in replies, which is its own kind of discipline.
entries.line: Hey I started a YANKEES SUCK chant in the stall next to you did you hear it?

entries.note: Posts like a man filing dispatches from a platform that doesn’t exist. Fake scoops, fake retirements, fake surveys, fake bumper-sticker giveaways — all deadpan enough that people reply seriously. The jokes are about posting itself, which is the most dangerous possible subject and he keeps getting away with it.
entries.line: SCOOP: Posting named the eighth deadly sin

entries.note: Works at Bluesky and posts as though nobody told her that. Bleak and horny in the same breath, then abruptly, completely serious about the thing that actually matters. The disclaimer in the bio is doing an enormous amount of work.
entries.line: the boys are never coming back to town. the boys have been dead for 10 years.

entries.note: Economical to the point of austerity. A handful of words, an emoji, and the sense that you’ve walked in on the end of a conversation you’d have enjoyed. The Everclear line is the whole style in one post: a joke that only works if you were also there.
entries.line: In the 2000s I was consuming a lot of Everclear. Everything was Wonderful

entries.note: Observational drift with a low-grade political fury underneath — hairlines, Quest bars, cyberstomachs, then a genuinely furious post about being gaslit as a nation, then back to the bike and the cat. The tonal whiplash is the point.
entries.line: We were all worried about the singularity, nobody expected the doublarity

entries.note: Range: an extended bit about Tolkien naming dwarves (“choin and groin and sloin”), hockey grievance, a genuinely useful argument for alt text, and a proposal to run the Costco hot dog guy for president. Funny and civic-minded at once, which is rarer than it sounds.
entries.line: keeping a positive attitude (eating batteries plus sign first)

entries.note: Chaotic in the good way — hockey, Netflix, drugs-and-candy drawers, and a joke about this very list that is funnier than the list deserves. Posts like someone with the TV on and no intention of turning it down.
entries.line: top 38 players who won’t shut up about the 1994 cult classic animated tv show ‘the critic’

entries.note: Builds entire absurd scenarios and then furnishes them. A POW forgetting morse code and resorting to charades; a Senate hearing derailed by the “Slow Toads-Infused Shrimped Kraut Crumb Lump.” The commitment to invented proper nouns is world-class.
entries.line: emulsions… very “enemies-to-lovers”

entries.note: Nominally a pizza account. In practice a one-person enthusiasm engine, mostly operating in the replies, who spent this contest openly campaigning for somebody else to win it. Made the list anyway, which is the most wholesome possible outcome.
entries.line: Folks! This is 1st place material 🥇 VOTE GREG! shitsky38.com/vote

entries.note: The most self-aware poster here by some distance — he wrote the definitive post about not having to post, and then kept posting, on purpose. Warren Zevon, ground beef orthodoxy, and the joy of blocking, held together by the voice of a man narrating his own decline with affection.
entries.line: i do not have to post every half-baked inane thought that blows through my weary, addled brain. i do it by choice. i can stop anytime i want

entries.note: “Middling jokes/existential dread” is the bio and also a complete and accurate review. Sparse lately, and what surfaces is small, exact irritation at modern life — the Netflix intro volume bit is a whole genre in one sentence.
entries.line: How did netflix know I would want to hear the intro song 100 decibels louder

entries.note: The menswear writer with 650,000 followers, on a list of shitposters, entirely on merit. He will explain the colour theory of tweed at length and with real scholarship, then post that some pilots are part of the furry community. The expertise is genuine, which is exactly what makes the swerves land.
entries.line: “why don’t men wear more color.” i only dress for the approval of dogs, who mostly see blue, white, gray, black, and brown in the way that we do, so i don’t wear other colors.

entries.note: “Garbage Bluesky. Flaming dumpster extraordinaire” is a mission statement and it is being honoured. Low volume, high impact, no interest whatsoever in defending the position afterwards.
entries.line: Yes , I am a bad person, next question.

entries.note: Horror, heavy lifting, and hospital-adjacent gallows humour, with the gallows load-bearing. The jokes about losing a patient sit a few posts from a genuinely sad one about a family asking for ivermectin because a chatbot told them to. Very funny, and not actually kidding.
entries.line: it is very easy to lose a patient, your honor

entries.note: Puns at 3am, addressed to a specific friend, in lowercase. “Real life is my alt” is the bio and the posting bears it out — this is someone using the site as a group chat and letting everyone else read over her shoulder.
entries.line: if scrooge’s lunch has been stolen he’s been hamburgled

entries.note: An Onion contributor writing with Onion precision — every post is a finished object with no wasted syllable, built on the pharmaceutical-ad cadence, the pickup line, the motivational poster. The craft is almost conspicuous.
entries.line: Ask your doctor if jeopardizing your health to make the rich richer is right for you

entries.note: A formalist. The two-hander script, the typographic pun, the wordplay that requires you to look at the letters rather than hear them. “Fall should be spelled fa//” only works written down, which is a joke about the medium as much as the word.
entries.line: DATE: what are you thinking about ME: fall should be spelled fa// DATE: ME: DATE: fell should be spelled fe_ _ *we kiss*

entries.note: Hockey, wordplay, and an unusually frank relationship with the posting compulsion. Half the feed is a running commentary on a goaltender named Bussi, which is exactly as sustainable as it sounds, and she is sustaining it.
entries.line: therapist: and what should we do when we’re feeling this way? me: keep posting 🙂‍↕️

entries.note: The quietest account on the list. Mostly short, warm replies to other people, punctuated occasionally by a line with no joke in it at all that lands harder than anything around it.
entries.line: I should learn how to heal without scabbing over.

entries.note: Essay-posting in a comic register, at a scale (320,000 followers) that makes it closer to a column. The mode is: describe the political economy accurately, and let the accuracy be the joke. Occasionally drops the comedy entirely and is just correct.
entries.line: Going to work now feels like doing homework after the teacher quit and told the class that education is fake.

entries.note: Committed to the bit of being a beaver spokesperson, and uses the persona as cover for real anger and real sincerity. Also campaigned for this list openly and shamelessly, which under the circumstances is arguably qualifying behaviour.
entries.line: HR says I need to stop referring to my coworkers as mortals. This feels like discrimination against high deities.

entries.note: “Horrors and hot dogs” — bone-saws and the Neutron Dance in the same sentence, cataract lenses collected as a hobby. The nemesis post is the thesis: an account about the specific social texture of being extremely online.
entries.line: If you don’t have a bluesky nemesis that doesn’t even know that they’re your bluesky nemesis, I hope you at least have friends in real life to keep you company.

entries.note: A 200,000-follower news-reaction account written entirely in lowercase by someone who keeps publicly confessing to typos. The register is “guy watching the same footage you are and saying the thing,” and the timing is what makes it work.
entries.line: i know it is a small thing but do these tech oligarchs not read before signing something from the unites states president

entries.note: Irish pun-craft, built and sanded. The bio admits that some posts are sculpture and some are farts, which is the most honest artistic statement on this page. The Deep Purple heckle is sculpture.
entries.line: In the UK aloe vera is just someone saying hello to their friend, Vera

entries.note: Warm, filthy, and communal — the rare poster whose replies are the draw. Turns their own divorce anniversary into a thread where everyone else gets to share something good. Shitposting as hospitality.
entries.line: Today is my divorceary. Send me one positive thing that happened to you along with a selfie/meme/both that’ll make me smile.

entries.note: Filth delivered with the timing of a grandmother telling a story. The Home Depot dream sequence escalates through three synonyms nobody needed and is better for each one.
entries.line: nana was quite secretive she always kept something up her sleeve (a tissue)

entries.note: Body-horror whimsy in a pleasant tone of voice. Cervical goblins, absorption rituals, escalator fatalities — all narrated as though describing a mildly interesting weekend. “My mom fucked a bat” is the bio and everything follows logically from it.
entries.line: It’s actually my 27th rodeo—I fucking love horses!

entries.note: Feral in the bio, feral in practice — affirmations, weights, hair, and a deep unwillingness to pretend. Alternates between genuine good-morning warmth and threatening to boil herself, which is a recognisable way to be alive right now.
entries.line: I made a salad for lunch and it tastes nothing like pizza.

entries.note: “I hat typos” is the bio, uncorrected, which tells you the whole operation. Absurdist observation with an unusually high hit rate, and a nihilist streak that surfaces as practical advice.
entries.line: Live every day like it’s your last. Key a cop car. Eat five hot dogs. Call your boss a taint. Who cares anymore?

entries.note: The smallest account on the list by followers and one of the angriest by volume — lyrics, invective, and cat-related co-custody. Sparse in the feed because most of the posting happens in other people’s replies.
entries.line: Blah, blah, blah…

entries.note: Has named himself the problem and proceeded accordingly. Raccoon persona, sell-out jokes, Ed Sheeran vendetta, and a deep understanding that acknowledging the engagement bait is itself engagement bait. Self-aware enough to be genuinely hard to insult.
entries.line: hating on me is just a weak attempt at engagement bait

entries.note: One perfect post about penguins and pebbles versus a man who put his bowl in the dishwasher, plus a feed full of kindness to strangers. Proof that you can make this list on precision rather than volume.
entries.line: Adélie penguins literally waddle across Antarctica to find the perfect pebble for their soulmate, but thanks for putting your dirty bowl in the dishwasher.

entries.note: A long-running parody account doing the hardest version of the form: satire of state communication that stays funny while being genuinely informative about the thing it mocks. “Parody, apparently” in the bio is doing heavy lifting.
entries.line: Do not believe anything until the Kremlin denies it™️

entries.note: Gentle surrealism about commerce and small irritations — greeting cards for Senate humiliations, a fitness tracker metric for stopping to smell the flowers, the Doritos CEO living on the property at Cool Ranch. Nothing mean anywhere in it.
entries.line: they call them Fun Size candy bars because it’s “fun” to eat a bunch of them and make your problems go away

entries.note: The most mysterious entry on the board — a feed of almost nothing, and then one unbroken stream-of-consciousness sentence that runs from hearing voices to monogamy without pausing for breath. Twenty-two people knew what they were voting for.
entries.line: Yeah I hear voices but they’re not yours so no witty banter or coffee or dinner or monogamy
